subject.title: [Bug]: `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` breaks `openai-codex` auth/keychain paths on macOS and can fail fresh runtime launch with `SecItemCopyMatching failed -50`

question: Should OpenClaw preserve the macOS `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` managed-service default and isolate/migrate Codex keychain auth reads, or change the process-wide macOS TLS default?
rationale: The source evidence crosses a TLS trust boundary and a credential/keychain boundary; without maintainer intent and live macOS proof, an automated fix could trade an auth failure for a managed-service TLS regression.

options.title: Scope The Auth Boundary
options.body: Keep the macOS service TLS default and add a focused Codex/OpenAI auth-keychain isolation or doctor migration path with macOS proof.

options.title: Change The TLS Default
options.body: Disable or override `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA` for broader launch paths, accepting the risk of regressing launchd TLS behavior that current code protects.

options.title: Prove Obsolete First
options.body: Close only after a maintainer demonstrates on macOS that current main no longer touches keychain-backed auth under the reported environment.

recommendation.title: Scope The Auth Boundary
recommendation.body: Keep the macOS service TLS default and add a focused Codex/OpenAI auth-keychain isolation or doctor migration path with macOS proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is tied to both the startup TLS planning and the Codex keychain/auth history needed for the boundary decision.
